SMTO-POL-0011 — A tool tried to ask the Model on its own, so SMTO stopped it

GUID: a5756c27-e7f2-49e2-845b-358948d21907
Slug: hidden-model-call-prohibited
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • A tool tried to get an extra answer from the Model outside the task's normal steps. SMTO blocks this so every Model decision stays under the task's controls. It's a fault in that tool, not in your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details in this panel. The details identify the tool that made the extra Model request, which is the part that needs fixing.
  2. Open the task in the conversation, check its tool calls, and note which Skill or tool was running when it stopped. Knowing the exact tool lets the person fixing it reproduce the problem.
  3. Leave this conversation as it is until the problem has been looked at. This error doesn't point to a fix you can make yourself, and the conversation's record helps find the cause.

What success looks like

  • After the person who manages SMTO fixes the tool, the same request finishes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied details and your note about the tool to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rephrase your request or change settings to get around this; that won't fix the tool and can hide the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A tool-side code path called NativeToolCallLLMClient.complete_json (or result_phase) while an execution budget already owned the semantic decision phase, so the nested structured model call was rejected.

What this means

  • An active execution budget already owns the semantic decision phase; nested structured inference from a tool boundary violates that ownership. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • An active execution budget already owns the semantic decision phase; nested structured inference from a tool boundary violates that ownership.

How to diagnose it

  • Locate the integration and active inference phase from the occurrence; distinguish an allowed result phase from a nested hidden model call.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Find the integration in the error's stack trace or error reference that called complete_json or result_phase inside tool execution while active_budget was set and active_phase was not (llm/native_tool_client.py, llm/budget.py). Move that inference into the supported model-decision phase or an explicitly owned result phase outside tool execution; changing prompts or disabling the guard is not a remedy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The integration performs deterministic tool work and routes necessary inference through its supported owning phase.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
